cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Warmth with a Countdown
cards.instruction: Perform increasing warmth with increasingly final language, as though every act of care might also be a goodbye.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Take my good teacup. I'll wrap it for you; I want you to have something from our afternoons here.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm only moving two streets away.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll put the saucer in as well. You can set a proper place for yourself when these afternoons are over.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We can still have tea together, can't we?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. You may bring it back whenever you like. Now choose the biscuit you want packed with it; I won't have our last tea in this room end with you going hungry.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 directs keepsake wrapping; A3 adds saucer and treats shared afternoons as ending; A5 grants future return while directing a final food choice, making care and farewell grow under A control.

responseLogic.evidence: A3 uses B2 nearby move to prepare a complete place there; A5 answers B4 future-tea request yes but frames present tea as last while increasing care.

relationship.evidence: B2 downplays distance and B4 seeks continuing connection, plausible person resisting overfinal farewell.

heightening.evidence: A5 uses B4 reassurance request to offer continued welcome and another caring act while refusing to relinquish farewell language.

specificity.evidence: A1 teacup and B2 move establish gifting context; saucer and biscuit are explicit added offers, not unprepared past events.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 long final meal-care line includes both warmth and finality; performable with sincere fussing.
